frontPage.headline: Anthropic IPO raises over $81 billion in largest offering on record, topping SpaceX
frontPage.summary: Anthropic priced its shares above the expected range and raised over $81 billion, the largest offering on record, CNBC reports. The stock is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on Thursday.
frontPage.whyItMatters: A listing of this size gives the market a public price for frontier-model economics, and it will shape how investors value the compute and cloud suppliers behind them.

frontPage.headline: Palo Alto inks $4.5 billion deal for AI startup Applied Compute, shares pop 7% on earnings
frontPage.summary: Palo Alto Networks agreed to a $4.5 billion deal for AI startup Applied Compute alongside its quarterly results. CNBC says shares rose 7% on the earnings report, and that the company has been buying companies steadily to meet demand for tools that defend against AI-driven attacks.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Security vendors are paying up for AI-native teams, which signals where agent and model-security controls will be built next.

frontPage.headline: Nvidia interim CEO Kress tells employees ‘let’s move forward’ at first all-hands meeting since Jensen Huang exit
frontPage.summary: Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress told employees at her first all-hands meeting since Jensen Huang's exit to move forward, and offered pay raises. CNBC reports the message was aimed at steadying staff after the leadership change.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Leadership continuity at the dominant AI-chip supplier matters to anyone planning GPU capacity and multi-year hardware roadmaps.

frontPage.headline: Microsoft’s Agent Framework PyPI package compromised to steal credentials
frontPage.summary: Attackers compromised Microsoft's official Agent Framework package on PyPI and published two malicious versions. BleepingComputer says the versions were built to steal cloud credentials and other sensitive data from developers' systems.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Agent frameworks now sit in the software supply chain with access to cloud credentials, so pinning, provenance checks and short-lived credentials in build environments are no longer optional.

frontPage.headline: European Commission confirms cyberattack, says hackers used AI tool
frontPage.summary: The European Commission confirmed a cyberattack and said the attackers used an AI tool. The Record, citing Politico, reports that CERT-EU identified the use of ARTEX, an open-source AI hacking platform that the FBI last week warned was used by both criminals and state-sponsored groups.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Defenders should assume automated, AI-assisted intrusion tooling is widely available, which shortens the time between disclosure and exploitation.

frontPage.headline: Trump, Xi, Putin End Historic Summit With Denunciation of Nuclear War
frontPage.summary: The leaders of the United States, China and Russia ended a first-ever summit in Shenzhen with a denunciation of nuclear war, the Wall Street Journal reports. The three also projected unity on energy security.
frontPage.whyItMatters: The meeting shifts the diplomatic backdrop for export controls, chip supply chains and energy prices that data-center planners depend on.

frontPage.headline: Trump says Americans should ‘relax’ as Washington scrambles to get to the bottom of outages
frontPage.summary: The Trump administration and Congress are rushing to address a series of technology failures over the past week, MarketWatch reports. Vice President J.D. Vance withdrew from an event on Wednesday to join meetings on the issue, and the president said Americans should relax.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Political attention to repeated outages raises the odds of reporting and resilience requirements for large cloud and software providers.

movers.reason: Reported quarterly results on the prior day; a Motley Fool headline cites accelerating growth and a $4.5 billion bet on the future of cybersecurity.
Sector-wide: a Barchart market wrap says Nvidia weakness pressured chipmakers in the prior session. This explains the close only, not the move at the open.
Zacks reports Robinhood added live IPO pricing tools ahead of Anthropic's listing; the headline does not say this drove the move at the open.

earningsDeepDive.results: Palo Alto Networks reported quarterly results on the prior day and agreed to a $4.5 billion deal for AI startup Applied Compute; CNBC says shares rose 7% on the report.
earningsDeepDive.guidance: Guidance figures were not in the material gathered for this edition.

items.headline: Anthropic IPO Lifts Mood in Markets
items.summary: The Nasdaq composite jumped on expectations of a pop in Anthropic's trading debut, the Wall Street Journal reports. The S&P 500 also climbed, setting up a day of gains after five consecutive down sessions.

items.headline: Why Micron, Intel and other AI stocks are getting a lift on Thursday
items.summary: MarketWatch says Micron, Intel and other AI stocks got a lift on Thursday, with Anthropic's IPO one reason. It also cites optimism about Texas's data-center landscape and a new buyback program from optical company Coherent.

items.headline: Intel signs first external customer for advanced 18A chips
items.summary: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said Wednesday that the company signed its first outside customer for its 18A chips, CNBC reports.
items.whyItMatters: An external customer is the first evidence that Intel's advanced process can win foundry business beyond its own products.

items.headline: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella calls Outlook outage a 'perfect storm.' Here's what went wrong
items.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella called the Outlook outage a 'perfect storm,' according to CNBC. The report notes Microsoft shares have dropped nearly 9% since closing at a record high on Nov. 4.

items.headline: Google Disrupts Its Search Advertising With Its Embrace of A.I.
items.summary: The New York Times reports Google's search advertising growth is slowing as AI becomes more prevalent, and that the company's embrace of AI is disrupting the business that long fueled it.
items.whyItMatters: The shift shows how AI answers can strain the revenue model of the company building them.

items.headline: Investors are rushing back into cybersecurity stocks after a string of outages. Here’s what to know before buying.
items.summary: MarketWatch says investors are returning to cybersecurity stocks after a string of outages, and that Wall Street has taken notice of the theme.

items.headline: Qualcomm offers test drive of its rack-scale Nvidia AI challenger
items.summary: Qualcomm is offering selected customers a test drive of its rack-scale Dragonfly AI200 on Cirrascale's cloud, The Register reports. The system is positioned as a challenger to Nvidia's AI racks.

items.headline: Non-profit claims 60% of Anthropic’s mapped US data center power demand is tied to natural gas
items.summary: A non-profit claims 60% of Anthropic's mapped US data center power demand is tied to natural gas, according to Data Center Dynamics. Anthropic says it is working to broaden its energy mix with renewable sources.

items.headline: Data center electricity use could double by 2030, IEA says
items.summary: Global electricity use by data centers could double by 2030 as the AI boom adds pressure to power grids, the IEA says, according to CNBC.

items.headline: Google turns to a volcano and rock-melting technology in a wild new bid to power AI
items.summary: Google has an agreement with Quaise on rock-melting geothermal technology to help power AI. A Bernstein analyst called it 'a bet on a first-of-a-kind technology,' MarketWatch reports.

items.headline: Inside the Codex sandbox
items.summary: OpenAI describes how Codex runs commands on a user's machine while enforcing the filesystem and network limits the user controls across macOS, Linux and Windows.
items.whyItMatters: A concrete reference for how a coding agent's sandbox boundary is drawn on each operating system.

items.headline: NVIDIA investigating Gentlemen ransomware breach claims
items.summary: NVIDIA is investigating claims of a security breach after the Gentlemen ransomware group listed the company on its dark web leak site, BleepingComputer reports.

items.headline: Critical NGINX ‘NGINX2Root’ bugs let attackers hijack servers
items.summary: Two critical NGINX vulnerabilities dubbed 'nginx2root' let unauthenticated attackers execute code remotely, BleepingComputer reports. Researchers demonstrated chaining the flaws with a Linux kernel bug to gain root.
items.whyItMatters: Edge proxies run in front of most services, so an unauthenticated flaw there is an inventory-and-patch problem for every team.

items.headline: How Cloudflare WAF helps protect against Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938)
items.summary: Cloudflare released six WAF managed rules for paid plans against Java4Shell, a critical memory-corruption flaw in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder that can lead to remote code execution. The rules log matching requests by default, and Cloudflare urges patching Java runtimes.

items.headline: Drupal patches critical RCE flaw, warns exploits may surface quickly
items.summary: The Drupal Security Team patched a critical remote code execution flaw that can let attackers take over sites, and warned that exploits may surface quickly, BleepingComputer reports.

items.headline: Russian charged with spying on Palantir employees for Moscow
items.summary: A Russian national recruited through Telegram has been charged in the United States with acting as a Moscow agent in a surveillance campaign targeting Palantir employees, The Record reports.

items.headline: Securities Regulators Warn That Slow Progress on Quantum Security is a Mistake
items.summary: The International Organization of Securities Commissions urged regulators and markets to prepare for quantum computers that could break the security protecting trades, payments and records, and warned progress may be too slow, The Quantum Insider reports.
items.whyItMatters: Post-quantum migration is now a regulatory expectation in finance, which will push inventory and crypto-agility work onto vendors.

items.headline: Scheduling the removal of the kube-proxy IPVS backend
items.summary: The Kubernetes project is scheduling removal of the kube-proxy ipvs backend. It says the kernel IPVS API proved a poor match for the Services API and never implemented all edge cases, while the nftables backend became GA in 1.33.
items.whyItMatters: Clusters still on IPVS mode need a migration plan to nftables before removal lands.

items.headline: Deterministic Simulation Testing
items.summary: Unmesh Joshi describes deterministic simulation testing, which replaces real clocks, networks and storage with simulated components driven by a single-threaded loop. It lets teams reproduce both hard failures and routine slowdowns such as latency spikes.

items.headline: Discord Rewrites Desktop and Mobile Clients in Rust Using Zed's GPU-Accelerated Rendering Framework
items.summary: Discord's CTO announced a rewrite of its desktop and mobile clients in Rust, moving away from Electron and React Native, InfoQ reports. Early results hint at significantly lower RAM use and faster boot.

items.headline: Producing Healthy Code with Artificial Intelligence Costs Fewer Tokens
items.summary: An InfoQ report says agentic AI can speed up velocity but the gains vanish within months as code complexity grows. It argues healthy code makes AI perform better and cost fewer tokens.

items.headline: STAT+: Epic Systems defends competitive practices, promises to let AI access its records
items.summary: Executives from Epic, the largest electronic health records vendor, defended its competitive practices in a panel at HLTH, STAT reports. They also said Epic will let AI access its records.

items.headline: STAT+: Merck, Isomorphic Labs partner to develop oncology drug candidates
items.summary: Merck and Isomorphic Labs said they are entering a research collaboration to discover small molecule candidates in oncology, STAT reports.

items.headline: HLTH 2026: Noom, Hims & Hers roll out peptide offerings
items.summary: Noom and Hims & Hers are launching peptide offerings as the federal government loosens restrictions on compounded treatments, Fierce Healthcare reports.

items.headline: Google acquires Seattle startup Howie and its AI scheduling assistant
items.summary: Google acquired Seattle startup Howie, an email-based AI scheduling assistant that raised a $6 million seed round last year. GeekWire says it will keep being built inside Google Labs.

items.headline: ‘Absurd ambition’: Pulumi expands into software delivery with AI agents that ship and fix code
items.summary: Pulumi launched Pulumi Delivery and Pulumi Agents, which let AI agents release software and fix cloud infrastructure, with teams deciding when people must sign off. GeekWire notes the company has about 100 employees, down from 130 last year.

items.headline: Battery startup Sila lands potential $1B Panasonic deal, plans Central Wash. expansion adding 500 jobs
items.summary: Sila announced a long-term agreement to supply Panasonic with silicon-carbon anode materials, potentially worth more than $1 billion. GeekWire says it requires expanding the Moses Lake, Wash. plant.

items.headline: Latest findings point to fuel supply, not Blue Origin’s engines, in loss of Amazon Leo satellites
items.summary: United Launch Alliance says preliminary findings point to the rocket's fuel supply rather than Blue Origin's engines in the loss of Amazon Leo satellites, GeekWire reports.

items.headline: Zeno Power makes progress on underwater power system that will eventually go nuclear
items.summary: Zeno Power made progress on an underwater power system that is intended to go nuclear later, with Pentagon funding, GeekWire reports.

items.headline: World Court Finds Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya
items.summary: The International Court of Justice found Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, the Wall Street Journal reports. It is the first time a state has been found legally responsible for seeking to destroy an ethnic or religious minority.

items.headline: Heightened hostilities in the Middle East reignite conflict
items.summary: The US and Iran traded strikes on military facilities, ending a two-month lull, Semafor reports.

items.headline: Putin vows 'far more painful' response to Ukraine's strikes on Crimean Bridge
items.summary: Vladimir Putin vowed a far more painful response to Ukraine's strikes on the Crimean Bridge, the BBC reports; he called it civilian infrastructure, which Kyiv disputes.

items.headline: How Nvidia Chips Ended Up Within Reach of China’s Military
items.summary: The New York Times reports Alibaba has used its AI computing technology to aid a lab with links to China's military, in the story behind the Nvidia spy saga.
items.whyItMatters: Chip-diversion cases like this drive tighter export controls that affect GPU supply and cloud access.

items.headline: Venezuela signs military deal with US less than a year after Maduro's removal
items.summary: Venezuela signed a military deal with the US less than a year after Maduro's removal, the BBC reports. The US defence secretary said the country has gone from an aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner.

items.headline: Putin touts Russia’s economy at APEC as Ukraine sends it toward a fuel crisis
items.summary: Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries have knocked out about half of Russia's refining output, analysts say, the Washington Post reports, darkening Russia's economic outlook.

items.headline: Sensex, Nifty surge over 1% as banks, auto stocks drive rally; Bank Nifty hits record high
items.summary: The Sensex and Nifty rose over 1% on Thursday, led by banks and autos, and the Bank Nifty hit a record high, The Hindu reports.

items.headline: EPFO relaxes withdrawal norms; lowers minimum balance requirement to 10%
items.summary: India's EPFO relaxed withdrawal norms, lowering the minimum balance requirement to 10% and introducing a systematic withdrawal plan that converts savings into a steady post-retirement stream, The Hindu reports.

items.headline: Coal India, ReNew, two others get initial nod for rare earth magnet sops
items.summary: Coal India, ReNew and two others received an initial nod for incentives under the rare earth magnet scheme, which targets processing raw materials from coastal monazite deposits into magnets, Mint reports.

items.headline: China’s proposed tech curbs put India’s solar manufacturing ambitions at risk
items.summary: India is assessing the effect of China's draft export rules on its solar manufacturing push toward 100 GW of wafer, ingot and polysilicon capacity by 2030, Mint reports. Manufacturers say investment plans remain intact but some projects could face delays.

items.headline: Tests as data: ensuring AI-generated code does what we want
items.summary: Matteo Vaccari argues that when AI writes both production and test code, customer tests become the primary contract between people and the AI, and that moving that contract into test data makes it easier to keep.
items.whyItMatters: A useful frame for design reviews of AI-assisted code: decide where the human-owned specification lives.

items.headline: Microsoft’s outage started with a fix
items.summary: LeadDev traces the Microsoft outage back to a fix, and to a bug that testing never caught.

items.headline: AI coding rules matter more than your model
items.summary: LeadDev argues that AI coding rules matter more than the model, and that teams should treat those rules like code.

items.headline: Software engineering after code becomes cheap with Satya Nadella
items.summary: Satya Nadella discusses AI's impact on software engineering, code verification and engineers' careers in a Pragmatic Engineer conversation.

learn.title: Why shuffle data deserves its own tier
learn.body:
Remote shuffle shows up when large batch jobs start failing for reasons unrelated to their own logic. In Spark and Flink, a shuffle moves intermediate data between stages. By default each worker writes its output to local disk and serves it to the next stage directly. That couples a job's reliability to the health of every worker it ran on: if one node is lost or slow, downstream tasks fail to fetch and the stage reruns.

LinkedIn's InfoQ-reported deployment of Apache Celeborn shows the alternative. A shared remote shuffle platform takes that intermediate data off the compute nodes and into a dedicated tier with its own storage, replication and data-plane tuning. Per the report, daily shuffle fetch failures fell from about 750 to 20, compute costs dropped 10%, runtimes improved 14%, and shuffle cost per task fell by nearly 90%.

The design lesson is separation of concerns by failure domain. Compute is elastic and disposable; intermediate data is not, because losing it forces recomputation. Putting data of different durability on different tiers lets each be sized, replicated and scaled for its own job. The same move appears in disaggregated storage, in write-ahead logs kept apart from query nodes, and in KV-cache tiers for inference.

The costs are real. A shared service is a new dependency and a new blast radius, so it needs capacity isolation between tenants, back-pressure and its own on-call. Replication buys durability by spending network and disk, and the network hop adds latency that local disk did not.

What to take into a design: identify state that is expensive to recompute and tied to machines you expect to lose, and ask whether it belongs on a tier built for it. Measure fetch failures and recomputation as first-class reliability metrics, since they are the symptom that tells you the coupling is hurting. And plan the shared tier as a product, with quotas, observability and a failure story of its own.

eating.tip: In a study summarized by NutritionFacts.org, swapping just 1% of animal protein for plant protein was associated with less age-related deficit accumulation. A practical takeaway is to shift protein sources gradually toward plant ones, such as lentils, beans and tofu.
